output.brief: The August dip is almost entirely explained by a cooling failure on floors 6-8. Chiller CH-2 was down from 4 to 19 August, and rooms reached 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1 and overall from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores recovered right after the repair. Floors 1-5 were flat, and their overall score moved only 0.1, which is within normal variation. Of 74 negative comments, 56 were about heat, all from floors 6-8. The new housekeeping contractor and the kiosks show no harm. Cleanliness, inspection pass rates, check-in scores and queue times were all steady, and the survey method was unchanged. So I advise against serving notice on Orrin or pulling the kiosks. The rate rise may have added a little to the value-for-money dip on floors 1-5, but that cannot be separated from the usual August seasonal dip. It is not worth reversing now. Next: reinstate the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spares on site, and write a cooling-outage guest-recovery protocol. Don't drop the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score. A return-stay offer to affected guests is reasonable, though they already received an apology and a credit. I'm fairly confident in this, and more evidence is unlikely to change these actions.
output.methodChoice: No further evidence collected; the initial evidence was decisive.
